The 2025 Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP) sets the City’s evaluation criteria and process for awarding Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC), a critical funding tool that the City utilizes to support affordable housing development.
LIHTC is a federal program that incentivizes public-private partnerships in affordable housing development by providing tax credits to investors in exchange for significant equity investments in qualified low-income rental housing developments. It is the most significant resource for the production and preservation of affordable rental housing in the United States today.
Additionally, DOH has released the
Architectural Technical Standards Manual (ATSM) version 4.1
, a policy document maintained by DOH that outlines design and contracting requirements for developers, architects, and general contractors building housing with City funds.
DOH worked closely with residents, advocates and developers to finalize the QAP this year. The draft was open for public comment until Thursday, May 15, 2025, at 4pm CT. DOH hosted a virtual public meeting on Tuesday May 6, 2025, at 1:30pm CT. Additionally, the Illinois Housing Council sponsored a QAP overview and feedback opportunity for developers on April 24, 2025.
If you have questions about the QAP, please email
DOHPPA@cityofchicago.org
.
*If you need to access this document in a language other than English, please email your request to
DOHPPA@cityofchicago.org
for a copy in your preferred language. Allow at least 10 business days for processing.

Notice: One-Time Administrative Adjustment to Full Project Application Deadline
Pursuant to the 2025 Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP), the Department is authorizing a one-time, Department-directed administrative adjustment to the Full Project Application deadline. In connection with this deadline adjustment, participants with existing Procorem Work Center access will be granted access to their Work Centers at approximately 9:00 a.m. Central Time on Tuesday, January 13, 2026, for the purpose of submitting application materials. Application materials may be submitted until 5:00 p.m. Central Time on Tuesday, January 13, 2026. At that time, all Procorem Work Centers will be converted to read-only access, and participants will no longer be able to upload, modify, or transmit any application materials. All application materials must be submitted exclusively through the applicable Procorem Work Centers. Any materials that are transmitted by other means, including but not limited to email, Dropbox, SharePoint, Google Drive, or similar file-sharing services, will not be accepted or considered part of a complete or timely submission.
